Implementation-relevant•FDA prescribing information•July 13, 2026

Lecanemab labeling adds subcutaneous treatment initiation

The July label permits weekly subcutaneous initiation, extending home-injection options beyond maintenance treatment.

Key label details: Subcutaneous starting dose is 500 mg weekly, as two 250 mg injections. After 18 months, continuing that regimen or transitioning to maintenance is permitted.

ManagementDisease-modifying treatment

Added September 7, 2026 · BLA 761375/S-001; FDA label reference 5833017

Evidence summaryDesign, results, and what changed

Thirty-second field brief

Route convenience changes delivery planning, while amyloid confirmation, early symptomatic eligibility and ARIA precautions remain.

Study design

Label update for initiation in MCI or mild AD dementia, with confirmed amyloid pathology.

Key label details

  • Subcutaneous starting dose is 500 mg weekly, as two 250 mg injections. After 18 months, continuing that regimen or transitioning to maintenance is permitted.
  • Subcutaneous maintenance is 360 mg weekly. The label specifies baseline MRI and monitoring after 1, 2, 3 and 6 months.

What changed

Subcutaneous dosing can begin at treatment initiation.

Strength of evidence

Authoritative dosing instructions; not a new head-to-head clinical-benefit trial.

Clinical and field impactInterpretation, implementation, and access

Clinical significance

Initiation and maintenance strengths must remain distinct.

Field medical relevance

Discuss delivery burden together with safety infrastructure.

Access or reimbursement relevance

FDA authorization is verified. Current supply, coverage and patient cost are not established here.

Likely questionsWhat you may hear and what the evidence supports
Does home dosing remove ARIA monitoring?
No. The boxed warning and MRI surveillance still apply.
Critique and limitationsBias, uncertainty, and missing evidence
  • This route change does not establish superior cognition outcomes or lower ARIA risk.
  • APOE ε4 homozygotes face higher ARIA risk; consult genotype counseling and risk instructions.

Primary source · Dated approval announcement

FDA. LEQEMBI/LEQEMBI IQLIK prescribing information. Revised July 2026. BLA 761375/S-001. Approval announced July 13, 2026.
